To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FGF, a polypeptide hormone which can stimulate 3T3 cell proliferation and differentiation, can also stimulate the uptake of amino acids and purines, and of pyrimidines.
FGF, in very low concentrations, can substitute for fresh serum to stimulate quiescent 10T1/2 and 3T3 cell transport system activities.
FGF can induce mitogenesis in serum‐depleted 3T3 cell cultures, and that this effect is accompanied by an increase in the uptake of several amino acids and purines, but not of glucose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of FGF as a substitute for serum to examine the transport system activation processes which occur in quiescent cells as they re‐initiate growth.
the use of FGF to induce mitosis in 10T½ cells and the use of these cells to study the early transport changes that accompany re‐initiation of growth.
a detailed examination of the transport system changes which are associated with the early stages of the growth response in quiescent cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FGF is a potent mitogen for quiescent 2‐2.5T3 cells, which is capable of stimulating transport system activities in a specific and temporal fashion.
, in terms of the early changes in transport activities, FGF is a very potent mitogen.
FGF, in the presence of insulin and dexamthasone, is an effective mitogen and that it is a potent stimulator of transport system activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FGF is a very potent growth factor, which, like other growth factors, has the capability to regulate cell transport activities.
, when quiescent cells are re‐stimulated by FGF, the earliest transport changes are the activation of the AIB and uridine uptake systems.
the transport system changes which occur during the early stages of the growth cycle in 3T 3 cells are regulated in a highly selective fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FGF can induce the transport system activation which occurs when quiescent cells are stimulated to grow.
FGF is a powerful tool for the study of the transport system activation processes which occur during cell growth stimulation.

FGF, in very small amounts, can induce transport system activation and cell proliferation in quiescent cells, and that the transport system activation and the mitogenic response to FGF are distinct and separate phenomena.
